reconcile.connective: Gill answers that Matthew alone names both animals because Jesus in fact used both, riding first the ass, then the colt.

discrepancy.connective: Ehrman argues Matthew misread Zechariah 9:9's Hebrew parallelism as two literal animals, calling the result 'a very peculiar memory' found in no other Gospel.

skeptic.name: Bart D. Ehrman
skeptic.work: Jesus Before the Gospels: How the Earliest Christians Remembered, Changed, and Invented Their Stories of the Savior
skeptic.attribution: Bart D. Ehrman, Jesus Before the Gospels (HarperOne, 2016)

excerpts.excerpt_text: The other evangelists only make mention of the colt, or young ass; but, no doubt, both were spoken of by Christ, and both were found by the disciples, the ass, and the colt by her, and both were brought away by them; and on both of them, very probably, Christ rode; first on one, and then on the other, as the prophecy hereby fulfilled seems to require, and as the sequel of the account shows.
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Directly answers why Mark and Luke mention only the colt while Matthew names both animals, proposing Jesus used both in succession so the accounts are compatible.

pd_work.resource: John W. Haley, An Examination of the Alleged Discrepancies of the Bible (1874)
pd_work.author: John W. Haley
pd_work.note: Haley quotes Matthew 21:2-3, Mark 11:2-3, and Luke 19:30-31 in parallel and treats the ass/colt wording as three independent witnesses each telling the story in his own way (p. 155).
